paper_title: VideoLLaMB Long-context Video Understanding with Recurrent Memory   Bridges
caption: GPU Memory Cost. We apply all the experiments on a single NVIDIA A800 GPU.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the GPU memory cost (in GB) for five different video understanding models as a function of the number of frames processed, ranging from 0 to 1000 frames on a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled "Memory (GB)", spans from 0 to 400 GB with major gridlines every 50 GB and minor gridlines every 10 GB. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Frames", is also linear and marked with tick labels at intervals of 200 frames (0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000). Five models are compared: VideoLLaMB (red line with circle markers), VideoLLaMB-R (brown line with circle markers), PLLaVA (green line with circle markers), LLaVA-NeXT (blue line with circle markers), and VideoLLAVA (purple line with circle markers). The VideoLLaMB model (red) shows a very low memory footprint, remaining nearly flat at approximately 5 GB across all frame counts. VideoLLaMB-R (brown) also exhibits a nearly constant memory usage, starting at about 5 GB and increasing slightly to around 25 GB at 1000 frames. PLLaVA (green) shows a gradual linear increase, starting at about 10 GB and rising to approximately 70 GB at 1000 frames. LLaVA-NeXT (blue) displays a steeper linear increase, starting at around 10 GB and reaching about 140 GB at 1000 frames. In contrast, VideoLLAVA (purple) demonstrates an extremely steep, near-exponential growth in memory usage, starting at approximately 20 GB at 0 frames and rising sharply to over 400 GB at 300 frames, with no data points shown beyond that point.
